answer.rationale: With 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, no buffer, and the incumbent refusing to reopen price, a full primary switch is the main TCO lever but carries unacceptable delivery risk this cycle; deferral is not available because the contract lapses. I intend to qualify the low-cost vendor as a second source in a guarded ramp rather than move primary volume immediately: this avoids a single point of failure, keeps the line supplied, creates credible pricing pressure, and stages a later primary shift if verification supports the prior low-cost-vendor outcome. This may not deliver the full 18% cut in-year, so residual value risk is flagged for next review.
